sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, rising from $15.4 billion to $25.8 billion [F1][F8][F145].
The path was not smooth: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022 and then fell 5.2% in FY2024 before recovering 9.8% in FY2025 [D131][D201][D236].
The FY2024 decline reflected lower storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,090 million and lower fuel cost recovery revenues of about $526 million [P34][P35].
The FY2025 rebound came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
FPL remains the dominant segment at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue, contributing 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth [D271][D273][D236].
FPL's revenue increase was driven by higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
Operating income grew 9.9% a year against revenue's 7.7%, while net income compounded at only 0.4% and diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year [F146][F145][F147][F149].
In FY2025 operating costs grew 0.2pp faster than revenue, at 10.0% [D257][D249].
NEER's FY2025 results rose on higher earnings from new investments, with 1,604 MW of wind, 2,859 MW of solar and 1,799 MW of battery storage added [P26].
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sat above the 30.3% window median but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high and far above the 15.5% FY2021 low [F24][D300][D299][D298].
The FY2025 margin was essentially flat, up 0.3pp, as operating costs grew 10.0% against 9.8% revenue growth [D247][D249][D236].
Depreciation and amortization rose $951 million in FY2025, mainly on higher amortization of deferred storm costs of about $1,090 million and higher plant in service [P16].
In FY2025 net margin of 26.5% sat 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin, with a -17.7% effective tax rate and $3.75 billion of other expense [F40][F24][D226][X64].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $12.5 billion covered net income 1.83x, in line with the 1.55x to 2.73x range across the window [F64][F32][D227][D157][D52].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% in FY2025 while net income fell 1.6% [D241][D238].
The shift from a net over-recovery to a net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million, mainly on higher fuel prices [P19].
Capital intensity is high: D&A was 25.5% of revenue in FY2025 and investing cash outflow reached $23.9 billion [D224][F72].
Total debt reached $95.0 billion in FY2025 against $2.81 billion of cash, a net debt position of $92.2 billion [D230][F96][D231].
Net cash of -357.4% of revenue ranked at the 0th percentile against a -228.4% utilities peer median (n=4) [D232][D314][D315].
Long-term debt grew 18.8% a year over the window while equity grew 6.9%, and the current ratio of 0.60x is the window high but still below 1.0x [F156][F157][F128][D305].
Free cash flow was consumed by $4.68 billion of dividends in FY2025, with no buybacks, while the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D233][D251].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x every year, at 0.60x in FY2025 against a 0.36x window low [F128][D304].
For a regulated utility with committed credit lines this is a working-capital convention rather than a liquidity crisis, but it leaves little current-asset cushion [F128].
Net cash has deteriorated for seven straight years, from -$34.3 billion in FY2018 to -$92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D231][R2].
Debt-funded growth is the model here, but the 18.8% annual debt growth against 6.9% equity growth steadily thins the balance sheet [F156][F157].
The effective tax rate swung from 5.6% in FY2024 to -17.7% in FY2025, a 23.3pp move [D191][D226][R4].
Clean energy tax credits drove the swing, so the tax line is a policy lever rather than a stable earnings contributor [P11].
Whether the FY2026 operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median, in the FY2026 10-K [D300].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -357.4% toward the -228.4% peer median, in the FY2026 10-K [D232][D315].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers from 1.83x toward the 2.73x FY2020 level, in the FY2026 10-K [D227][D52].
